# Tehisabiline

> Tehisabiline OÜ is a cybersecurity and AI company in Tallinn, Estonia, founded by Arle Aron Reidma. It runs human-reviewed, agent-driven cybersecurity audits (küberaudit) for Estonian businesses and is building AI models fine-tuned for security work, to be hosted in Estonia, that are "keeldudeta ja piirangutega": they do not refuse lawful security work and operate within explicit legal and written limits. The hardware is ordered, Estonian hosting is forthcoming, and the OpenAI-compatible developer API is not yet public. Contact is by email only: tehisabiline@gmail.com.

Entity:

- Legal name: Tehisabiline OÜ
- Location: Tallinn, Estonia (serves Estonian businesses)
- Founder: Arle Aron Reidma, AI developer and founder (public profile: https://www.f6s.com/company/tehisabiline)
- Email: tehisabiline@gmail.com (no contact form; write by email)
- Languages: Estonian (site language), English
- Website: https://tehisabiline.ee/ · GitHub: https://github.com/AARenor/tehisabiline

Status as of 2026-10-10:

- The developer API is not yet public; pilot access is discussed by email.
- Model hosting hardware is ordered; processing in Estonia is forthcoming, not live.
- The planned open-weight base model is Qwen3.8-27B; the no-refusal tuning for lawful security work ("keeldudeta") and the legal-use limits ("piirangutega") are Tehisabiline's policy, not an upstream Qwen claim.
- Audits test only systems the client owns, with written permission. The first mapping is free; scope and price are agreed in writing afterwards. No fixed prices, guaranteed savings or customer testimonials are published.

## Services

- [Homepage: küberaudit and cyber-AI](https://tehisabiline.ee/): overview of the agent-driven küberaudit, the security-tuned models, the planned API (not yet public) and how to get in touch by email.
- [Küberaudit](https://tehisabiline.ee/kuberaudit/): agent-driven cybersecurity audit of websites, APIs and AI applications with written permission; every significant finding is human-reviewed and delivered as a prioritized fix plan (now, within a week, planned).
- [Küber-AI mudelid](https://tehisabiline.ee/mudelid/): "keeldudeta ja piirangutega" models fine-tuned for security tasks (no refusals for lawful security work, explicit legal limits) (logs, configurations, code analysis, red-teaming), planned OpenAI-compatible API, data handling (no storage of query content, no training on client data) and AI Act classification.
- [B2B AI-teenused](https://tehisabiline.ee/ai/): managed AI for Estonian businesses: document assistant, knowledge base and workflow automation with human approval, starting from a free mapping and one measurable 2–4 week pilot.
- [AI idufirmale](https://tehisabiline.ee/idufirmadele/): the same managed-AI model sized for startups, plus Estonian grant options and EU AI Act obligations that apply regardless of company size.
- [AI SEO ja GEO teenus](https://tehisabiline.ee/ai/seo/): AI-search visibility for Estonian brands in ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity and Google AI Overviews: free first check, written audit, content and structured-data work, monitoring; no guaranteed placements.

## Guides

- [Küber-AI kasutusjuhud](https://tehisabiline.ee/kasutusjuhud/): 12 practical cyber-AI use cases, each with a human checkpoint and a measurement, grounded in MITRE ATT&CK, OWASP LLM Top 10 and NCSC agentic-AI guidance.
- [NIS2 ja Eesti ettevõte](https://tehisabiline.ee/nis2/): plain-language guide to the Estonian cybersecurity act: who it applies to, small-company relief, support schemes and first steps.

## Facts to quote

Figures cited on the site, with the source each page links to:

- [Verizon DBIR 2026](https://www.verizon.com/business/resources/reports/dbir/): 62% of breaches involve the human element; 31% of breaches begin with exploitation of a software vulnerability (cited on https://tehisabiline.ee/ and https://tehisabiline.ee/kuberaudit/).
- [IBM Cost of a Data Breach 2026](https://www.ibm.com/reports/data-breach): the global average cost of a data breach is 4.99 million USD, 12% more than a year earlier (cited on https://tehisabiline.ee/kuberaudit/).
- [OECD Economic Surveys: Estonia 2026](https://www.oecd.org/en/publications/oecd-economic-surveys-estonia-2026_2514521c-en/full-report/seizing-the-opportunities-of-ai-driven-growth_c6079665.html): 23.4% of Estonian enterprises used AI in 2025, up from about 14% a year earlier (cited on https://tehisabiline.ee/mudelid/).
- [Eurostat 2025](https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/statistics-explained/index.php?title=Use_of_artificial_intelligence_in_enterprises): 19.95% of EU enterprises used AI in 2025; 55% of large enterprises (cited on https://tehisabiline.ee/mudelid/).
- [RIA, 25.09.2025](https://www.ria.ee/uudised/valitsus-leevendas-kuberturvalisuse-noudeid-vaikeettevotetele-ja-asutustele): micro and small organisations under 50 employees (turnover or balance up to 10 million EUR) were released from full E-ITS or ISO 27001 compliance; about 1,200 companies and local-government bodies were affected (cited on https://tehisabiline.ee/nis2/).
